title: Delhi-NCR Imposes GRAP-1 Curbs as Air Quality Slips to Poor
excerpt: CAQM invoked GRAP Stage-I across Delhi-NCR on October 21 after Delhi's AQI rose from 179 to 244, with poor air forecast to continue in coming days.
body:
• The Commission for Air Quality Management imposed GRAP Stage-I across Delhi-NCR on October 21 with immediate effect as Delhi's AQI rose to 244.
  • Delhi's AQI jumped from 179 (moderate) on October 20 to 244 (poor) at 2 p.m. on October 21; IMD and IITM forecast poor air to continue in coming days.
  • GRAP-1 bans coal and firewood in tandoors at hotels, restaurants and open eateries, and restricts diesel generators to emergency and essential use.
  • For residents and businesses: expect mechanised sweeping, water sprinkling, stricter construction dust checks and a ban on open waste burning — comply with site dust norms and avoid burning waste.

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Wednesday imposed Stage-I measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR, after Delhi's air quality slipped into the 'poor' category. The decision took effect immediately.

"The Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi which was observed 179 (Moderate category) on October 20, has exhibited a sharp rise with AQI of 244 at 2 pm on October 21 (Poor category)," the CAQM said in a statement reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. The CAQM sub-committee reviewed the air quality scenario and the forecast before invoking the stage, according to LatestLY.

Why the curbs were triggered now

GRAP is a set of emergency measures that apply in stages as air quality worsens. Stage-I applies when the AQI is between 201 and 300, the 'poor' range. Stage-II applies at 301 to 400, Stage-III at 401 to 450, and Stage-IV above 450. Delhi crossed the Stage-I threshold in a single day, moving from moderate to poor.

The forecast matters as much as the single reading. The CAQM said forecasts by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) predicted the AQI would remain in the 'poor' category in the coming days. Acting at Stage-I is intended to prevent a further slide toward 'very poor' rather than wait for it.

What GRAP-1 actually restricts

Under GRAP-1, the use of coal and firewood as fuel in tandoors in hotels, restaurants and open eateries is banned. Diesel generator sets are allowed only for emergency or essential situations. Those are the most visible bans for businesses and residents.

The wider package is about dust and waste. Agencies have been directed to carry out mechanised sweeping of roads and water sprinkling, ensure regular lifting of municipal and construction waste, enforce a ban on open waste burning, and apply dust-mitigation norms at construction and demolition sites. Implementing agencies across the NCR have been told to keep strict vigil, intensify measures under the GRAP schedule, and ensure the AQI does not slip further.

What this means for people in Delhi-NCR

For households, there is no ban on private vehicles or on leaving home under Stage-I, but residents are asked to follow the citizen charter under GRAP Stage-I, as the CAQM order noted. For eateries, the tandoor rule means switching to electricity, gas or other clean fuel where coal or firewood was used. For builders and contractors, dust control — covering material, sprinkling and proper disposal of debris — will be checked more closely, and violations can draw enforcement action.

For diaspora families with parents or relatives in Delhi-NCR, the practical point is timing: air is forecast to stay poor in the coming days, so outdoor exertion for older relatives and children is better limited on high-AQI mornings, and travel plans should allow for the start of the winter pollution season. Check the daily AQI before scheduling outdoor events.

What happens next

The CAQM sub-committee said it would keep a close watch on air quality and review the situation from time to time, depending on Delhi's AQI and the IMD/IITM forecast. If the AQI rises into the 301-400 range, Stage-II measures would follow, with stricter curbs. If it falls back below 201 and stays there, Stage-I can be lifted. For now, the first curbs of the season are in force across the entire NCR.
